_comment: Writings found on hunts (game/library.py). ALL TITLES AND TEXTS ARE PLACEHOLDERS that only restate lore the user has already given; replace them with the real lore. look: what it is before it's read (see looks). difficulty 1-6: the Scholarship rank needed to read it (one rank short: you can't read it, but learn from trying). teaches (optional; user, 2026-11-19): keyword ids for the Wayfinder that reading it teaches, if the Hunter's Scholarship is up to its difficulty (most writings teach none: they're lore). PLACEHOLDERS: three writings teach a word. regions: optional, where it can turn up: a land style (caves, ruins, forest), a keyword id, or a place id (danger/land/feature); empty = anywhere. find_chance: the chance each area of a hunt holds a writing. pay_per_difficulty: what the Academy librarian pays for one (x difficulty), doubled if you've read it yourself. A writing that's shelved in the library, or that someone has (bag, stash, the city), doesn't turn up again.

torn_page.name: torn page
torn_page.description: A page torn from a book, written

journal.name: weathered journal
journal.description: A small journal, swollen with damp, written

letter.name: folded letter
letter.description: A letter, folded small and sealed with wax, written

tablet.name: inscribed tablet
tablet.description: A slab of stone, palm-sized, carved

scroll.name: rolled scroll
scroll.description: A tight roll of thin hide, written

hunters_tally.title: A Hunter's tally
hunters_tally.text: A list, in a hurried hand: hunts, and what came of them. Most lines end the same way: a broken artifact carried home, and what the workshop paid. A few lines end in nothing at all. The last line is unfinished.

ordinal_days.title: A letter about the holidays
ordinal_days.text: Written to a friend: 'Emu, Lagau, Erku, Maforu, Nusu, Senu, Riu, Dymiu, Neu, and round again, until the Duel is over. Then four days with no names at all, and we'll drink to having lived through it, and ready ourselves for the next. Come home for them, if you can.'

crumbling_gate_notes.title: Notes from beyond the Crumbling Gate
crumbling_gate_notes.text: Field notes. East through the Crumbling Gate, into the ruins. The writer counts the fallen walls, and the creatures among them, and how far they dared go. The entries grow shorter towards the end.

founding_record.title: A founding record
founding_record.text: Carved: in the hundred and twentieth Turn, a city was founded nine kilometres south of the Tower, and named Bytorsskug. The rest of the stone is worn smooth.

chorus_winds.title: On the Chorus Winds
chorus_winds.text: The Winds blow about the Tower and hold the miasma back, out to ninety-nine kilometres from it: the Brisering. Beyond, there is only the miasma, and the Tower's artifacts fall silent there unless one carries the Winds along in a windcatcher.

artificers_letter.title: A letter to the Artificers' Guild
artificers_letter.text: A request to be examined for the rank of Journeyman. The writer lists the artifacts they have mended, and the Master they apprenticed under, and asks when the board next sits.

glass_and_coin.title: Glass and coin
glass_and_coin.text: The shards that pass from hand to hand in the markets were, once, true pieces of windcatcher glass. The writer seems to think this important, and spends the rest of the scroll arguing about it with someone who isn't there.

tower_measurements.title: Measurements of Myligast
tower_measurements.text: Myligast: nine kilometres across at its foot. Its height: none could be measured; it does not end. A way in: none found. The writer has underlined that last line twice.

count_of_turns.title: A count of Turns
count_of_turns.text: A long column of marks, one for every Turn since the first was counted, each a Light Duel and a Dark Duel with holidays between. The column stops at two hundred and ten.

untranslated_fragment.title: An untranslated fragment
untranslated_fragment.text: Only a few words can be made out with any confidence: the Tower, the Winds, and one more that no two scholars at the Academy read the same way. The rest waits for a better scholar.

selda_writing.title: A cartographer's complaint
selda_writing.text: A letter never sent, folded small. Its writer mapped the caves north of Bytorsskug for the Academy, and spends most of a page complaining: the damp, the dark, the Academy's slowness to pay. Lower down the hand grows unsteady. One stretch of the caves, they write, felt wrong: the air too still, the dark too thick, light that wouldn't carry. "Our guide had a name for it from the Wayfinder's words: Broken Promise. I asked her why. She said: because it looks like a way through, and it isn't." The letter breaks off there. Handed in to the library by Selda Fencer Hunters. (Chapter 1; the assistant's draft.)
